title: Call Stack Check
description: Trace push/pop of stack frames for synchronous calls.

questions.explanation: `first` waits while `second` runs on top of the stack. `after second` prints only after `second` returns.

questions.prompt: At the exact moment `"second"` prints in the first example, which frame is on top of the call stack?
questions.explanation: `second` is the currently executing frame. `first` is waiting underneath until `second` returns.

questions.prompt: What happens when a function recursively calls itself with no exit condition?

options.text: The event loop skips it and continues
It becomes a microtask and waits
The call stack grows until `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
Node automatically moves it to a worker thread

questions.explanation: Infinite recursion keeps pushing frames until the engine throws a maximum call stack size error.

questions.prompt: Why can a `setTimeout` callback **not** jump onto the call stack while `first()` is still running?

options.text: Timers are ignored until the process exits
Current synchronous frames must finish (pop) before the event loop runs queued callbacks
Because Promise microtasks always cancel timers

questions.explanation: Scheduled callbacks wait until the current synchronous stack is clear. The event loop cannot interleave them mid-call-chain.
